24 An observer is situated at the top of a tall tower. An aeroplane emitting sound at a frequency of
1000 Hz approaches the observer at a speed of 165 m s–1.
The speed of sound is 330 m s–1.
What is the frequency of the sound received by the observer?
A
330 Hz
B
667 Hz
C
1000 Hz
D
2000 Hz

hints: Notice the aeroplane is approaching the stationary observer at $165 \text{m s}^{-1}$, which is exactly half the speed of sound $330 \text{m s}^{-1}$.

Recall that motion toward the observer compresses the sound waves, so the observed wavelength $\lambda_o$ is shorter than the emitted wavelength and the observed frequency must be greater than $1000 \text{Hz}$.
Use $f_o = f_s \times v/(v - v_s)$ for an approaching source and calculate $330/(330-165)$ times $1000 \text{Hz}$.
walkthrough: Identify the data: source frequency $f_s = 1000 \text{Hz}$, source speed $v_s = 165 \text{m s}^{-1}$ toward the observer, wave speed $v = 330 \text{m s}^{-1}$, observer stationary.

State the Doppler rule: when the source moves toward the observer the wavefronts are bunched up, so observed wavelength $\lambda_o = (v - v_s)/f_s$ is smaller and observed frequency $f_o = v/\lambda_o$ is larger.
Set up the approaching-source equation $f_o = f_s \times v/(v - v_s)$.
Substitute with units: $f_o = 1000 \text{Hz} \times 330 \text{m s}^{-1}/(330 \text{m s}^{-1} - 165 \text{m s}^{-1}) = 1000 \text{Hz} \times 330/165$.
Calculate the factor: $330/165 = 2.0$, so $f_o = 2000 \text{Hz}$ with unit $\text{Hz}$ as required.

A.explanation: 330 Hz confuses the speed of sound $330 \text{m s}^{-1}$ with the observed frequency; the approaching source must increase the $1000 \text{Hz}$ frequency, not reduce it.

B.explanation: 667 Hz is $1000 \times 330/(330+165)$ and is the frequency for a source receding at $165 \text{m s}^{-1}$; here the aeroplane is approaching so the wavelength is shortened.

C.explanation: 1000 Hz would mean no Doppler shift, which ignores that the $165 \text{m s}^{-1}$ approach crowds successive wavefronts closer together in front of the source.

D.explanation: For an approaching source $f_o = f_s v/(v-v_s) = 1000 \times 330/165 = 2000 \text{Hz}$, so the observed frequency is doubled.
